Water: FlowCast, the collection's ungauged network, beats the law (MAE 0.112 vs 0.129 on 619 basins). The law beats Budyko-Fu (0.141-0.154). In snowy basins (f_s > 0.3, 88 basins) every method is poor (law 0.22). All rows share ERA5-Land forcing, which under-catches mountain precipitation: 50 basins carry more water out than ERA5 says falls in.

Fire: FireSim's own law over-predicts real next-day growth a median 36 times (bias +1.56 decades). The released law survives only because the dev gate cut it down to a saturating curve. Over all fire-days it loses to FireData's yesterday's-growth baseline (1.15 vs 0.67 mean |log₁₀|); on growth days it is the best row (0.69 vs FireCast 0.76). FireSim has no fire persistence (stalls, burnout), the platform's known gap. Slope was not an input: real exam fires have no landscape.

Grid inertia: GridSim's raw GB fleets commit about 4.5 s of inertia per MW of demand where NESO's outturn shows about 7, so the law is 33 % low (MdAPE) and loses to 7 s × demand (15.1 %) and to the dev median (24 %). Its ranking is the best of all rows (ρ 0.975).

Grid nadir: the loss labels are noisy (REMIT/FUELINST matches); 148 events. The dev gate had only 4 events, one of them (9 Aug 2019) a cascade. The 68 % bar (±0.31 Hz) is far too wide: it covers 100 % of exam events.

Homes: the law loses to the dumb dev median (MdAPE 39.3 % vs 33.4 %) and to a log-linear fit on dev (26.6 %). BuildingSim's homes are about 1.4 times too energy-intensive at physics 1.0; 1.4 fixes the median but not the spread. RECS energy is EIA's billing-based estimate, and home-to-home variation (occupants, setpoints) is not in the inputs.

Road: the law loses to EnergyNet everywhere and, on real VED trips, to RoadData's MOVES-like and window-label baselines (18.6 % against 11.8 % and 14.1 %). It beats road-load on EPA petrol and hybrid tests (17.3 % and 13.1 % against 25.0 % and 19.6 %) and loses to it on electric cars: it reads the 2 VED Leafs 42 % low and EPA BEVs 42 % high, one exponent for every electric car. RoadSim's own shorter law (p2-c10) beats the released one on VED petrol (14.0 %) and on EPA (15.1 %); the dev gate (14 dev cars, 1,178 EPA dev tests) picked the longer law. Real CdA and Crr are class defaults on VED (EPA: from the road-load coefficients); VED fuel is MAF-estimated for most cars. Exam run 1 mis-scaled EnergyNet's VED rows (units); its published values on the same trips are shown instead.

Method: one search per physics version, time-boxed at 4-7 minutes on a shared core; another seed can give a different front. Dev sets are small (4 grid events, 40 fires, 52 basins), so the gate is coarse. The road law (RoadSim trip energy) was not built in this batch.
